title: The Reichstag, Before & After: Quick Summary
items: **The Reichstag is the same building through every chapter of modern German history.** Read it before and after and you get imperial parliament, the 1933 fire, a 1945 ruin, thirty divided-city years, and today's glass-domed home of German democracy, all in one facade.
**Built 1884 to 1894** to plans by Paul Wallot, with the bronze words **Dem Deutschen Volke** (To the German People) fixed above the entrance in **1916**, more than twenty years after it opened.

**The fire came on 27 February 1933.** It gutted the chamber and the original dome, and the Nazis used it to push through the decree that suspended civil liberties and cleared the way for dictatorship.

**In 1945 it became the prize of the Battle of Berlin.** Soviet soldiers raised a flag over the ruin (Yevgeny Khaldei's famous photo, 2 May 1945) and left graffiti on the inner walls. Shrapnel scars and that **Cyrillic graffiti** were deliberately kept in the 1990s rebuild.

**For thirty years it was a domeless ruin on the edge of the Wall,** parliament sitting in Bonn. In 1995 Christo and Jeanne-Claude wrapped the whole building in silver fabric and about five million people came.

**Norman Foster's glass dome opened in 1999** and the Bundestag returned on 19 April 1999. The dome is **free but needs a booking in advance** at bundestag.de, and you show the passport or ID you registered with.
